thesis_text:
Bottom line: for Datadog (Software Engineering (SWE), entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-10-12 with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. High, centralized bar: practical coding depth plus system design and a behavioral round that also probes past technical work. This is a qualitative synthesis, not a measured pass rate — Datadog publishes no applicant-to-offer rate in the fetched sources.

Who gets in (sample N=not available — curated-qualitative record, as of 2026-10-12):
- This CIR is curated-qualitative: no population sample exists for it yet, so there are no percentages to show. What follows is the reported pattern from public sources, labeled as such.
Known biases of this data: Survivorship bias: public interview guides reflect people who reached or completed loops, not rejected applicants.; Self-report bias: interviewing.io content is based on conversations with engineers and cross-checked anecdotes, not Datadog HR data.; Official careers pages are employer marketing and describe the intended process, which may differ by team, level and region.; No H-1B LCA, university-outcome or licensed population data was fetched in this pass; sponsorship and school patterns are therefore unstated, not negative findings.. We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).

What Datadog says it screens for vs what the record shows:
Stated: Official candidate page: one interview step is expected to happen in person. Official candidate page: AI tools are restricted during interviews; misuse or non-disclosure can lead to disqualification. Engineer-reported: system-design performance is used for leveling, and shallow design answers can result in a down-level.

This is a qualitative synthesis, not a measured pass rate — Datadog publishes no applicant-to-offer rate in the fetched sources. | gap | fix: Land one real internship or role at a smaller, reachable employer first — the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns.
- projects: you — no projects on file | cohort — Revealed screen in this CIR: evidence of building or analyzing real things (see screening_signals.revealed). | gap | fix: Ship one project that solves a messy real problem for a real user, and document it.
- skills: you — no skills on file | cohort — not on file | unknown

- authorization: you — not on file | cohort — Sponsorship history is a matter of public record (DOL H-1B LCA filings); this CIR states only what its sources support, and immigration specifics go to the school's international office (§4.8 Q26 — not legal advice). | gap | fix: Confirm sponsorship for this exact role family before investing a season of prep; target employers with a filing history for the role.

The plan:
Next 30 days:
- Confirm this cycle's application window and deadlines for Datadog on the official careers page — dates move, and this CIR's cadence fact is the starting point, not the truth (§3.3). (by 2026-10-19)
- Apply to a first, reachable rung: a smaller employer in the same role family (the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns). Volume plus follow-up is the play. (by 2026-10-26)
- Ship the first version of one real project and write it up publicly. (by 2026-11-11)
- Build the coffee-chat target list from this CIR's entry routes: recent hires in the same role family, alumni of your school, people one rung up the ladder. (by 2026-10-22)
This semester:
- Convert the semester into signal: one internship or substantial project, one visible leadership or club role in the field, and interview reps on a weekly schedule.
- Run the coffee-chat list: short, specific asks; every conversation ends with a follow-up you actually send.
This year:
